  <circle class="nd" cx="120" cy="60" r="15"/><text class="lbl-w" x="120" y="65">M</text>

  <line class="lg" x1="245" y1="60" x2="280" y2="60"/>
  <text class="lbl" x="62" y="48">i</text>

  <line class="lg" x1="445" y1="60" x2="410" y2="60"/>
  <line class="lg" x1="475" y1="60" x2="510" y2="60"/>

</svg>
:::

- Joined legs = sum over shared index
- Dangling legs = indices of result
- Closed loop = trace, no free legs, so a number
- Whole course built from two moves: place node, join leg

## Penrose Diagrams: Vocabulary and Cost

- Identity: bare line. Copy/$\delta$ tensor: branching node
- Isometry: shaded node, $A^\dagger A = \mathbb{1}$
- Convention: physical legs down, bonds horizontal

::: {.callout-tip}
Contraction **order** is visible in the diagram, and order sets the cost.
Chain of $n$ rank-3 tensors: sequential $O(n\chi^3)$, naive $O(2^n)$.
:::

## Two Communities, One Object

| Quantum many-body | Numerical analysis |
|---|---|
| Matrix product state (MPS) | Tensor train (TT) |
| Bond dimension $\chi$ | TT-rank |
| Entanglement across a cut | Singular-value decay |
| DMRG sweep | Alternating least squares |

- Both vocabularies appear in this course and in the source papers
- Reviews: [@orus2014] physics side, [@oseledets2011] numerics side

## The Curse of Dimensionality

- Mesh of $N = 2^n$ points per dimension: $2^{nd}$ unknowns in $d$ dimensions
- $1024^3$ mesh $= 2^{30} \approx 10^9$ unknowns per field per timestep
- 3D DNS needs $\sim\mathrm{Re}^{9/4}$ degrees of freedom
- Aircraft at cruise: $\mathrm{Re}\sim10^7$, so $\sim10^{16}$ dof. Exascale does not close this

## Why Structure Is the Only Way Out

- Finite differences, volumes, elements: none change the scaling
- Every classical escape exploits structure: adaptive meshes, multigrid, spectral, POD
- Tensor-network claim: a smooth multiscale field is not an arbitrary point in $\mathbb{R}^{2^n}$. It sits on a manifold of size $O(n\chi^2)$
- Price: exact linear algebra becomes approximate arithmetic, truncated every step

::: tn
<svg viewBox="0 0 640 150" role="img" aria-label="Matrix product state as a chain of rank-3 tensors with physical legs down and bonds between">
  <line class="bd" x1="95" y1="55" x2="545" y2="55"/>

  <circle class="nd" cx="335" cy="55" r="15"/><text class="lbl-w" x="335" y="60">A₃</text>
  <circle class="nd" cx="455" cy="55" r="15"/><text class="lbl-w" x="455" y="60">…</text>
  <circle class="nd" cx="545" cy="55" r="15"/><text class="lbl-w" x="545" y="60">Aₙ</text>
  <line class="lg" x1="95" y1="70" x2="95" y2="100"/>
  <line class="lg" x1="215" y1="70" x2="215" y2="100"/>
  <line class="lg" x1="335" y1="70" x2="335" y2="100"/>
  <line class="lg" x1="455" y1="70" x2="455" y2="100"/>
  <line class="lg" x1="545" y1="70" x2="545" y2="100"/>
  <text class="lbl" x="95" y="122">i₁</text>
  <text class="lbl" x="215" y="122">i₂</text>
  <text class="lbl" x="335" y="122">i₃</text>
  <text class="lbl" x="455" y="122">…</text>
  <text class="lbl" x="545" y="122">iₙ</text>
  <text class="lbl-sm" x="155" y="42">χ</text>
  <text class="lbl-sm" x="275" y="42">χ</text>
  <text class="lbl-sm" x="395" y="42">χ</text>
</svg>
:::

$$v_{i_1 i_2 \cdots i_n} = A^{(i_1)}_1 A^{(i_2)}_2 \cdots A^{(i_n)}_n$$

- $\chi$ = matrix size on the bonds. Parameters $\le 2n\chi^2$, not $2^n$
- Exponential compression **only while $\chi$ stays bounded**

## Why an MPS Can Work at All

::: tn
<svg viewBox="0 0 620 120" role="img" aria-label="Cutting an MPS chain at one bond; the bond dimension there is the rank across the cut">
  <line class="bd" x1="80" y1="45" x2="540" y2="45"/>
  <circle class="nd" cx="80" cy="45" r="13"/>
  <circle class="nd" cx="185" cy="45" r="13"/>
  <circle class="nd" cx="290" cy="45" r="13"/>
  <circle class="nd" cx="395" cy="45" r="13"/>
  <circle class="nd" cx="500" cy="45" r="13"/>
  <circle class="nd" cx="540" cy="45" r="13"/>
  <line class="cut" x1="240" y1="10" x2="240" y2="85"/>
  <text class="lbl" x="240" y="105">cut k</text>
  <text class="lbl-sm" x="140" y="30">left half</text>
  <text class="lbl-sm" x="400" y="30">right half</text>
</svg>
:::

- Bond dimension at cut $k$ = rank of $v$ reshaped across that cut
- Rank set by singular-value decay = entanglement between halves
- 1D local Hamiltonians obey an **area law**: bound independent of $n$ [@hastings2007]
- Smooth multiscale functions behave the same. Noise and random data do not

## Building an MPS: TT-SVD

::: tn
<svg viewBox="0 0 640 130" role="img" aria-label="Sequential SVD splitting one tensor off the chain at each step">
  <rect class="box" x="40" y="30" width="90" height="50" rx="4"/>
  <text class="lbl" x="85" y="60">v</text>
  <text class="lbl" x="85" y="105">reshape</text>
  <text class="lbl" x="165" y="60">⇒</text>
  <circle class="nd" cx="235" cy="55" r="14"/>
  <rect class="box" x="270" y="30" width="80" height="50" rx="4"/>
  <line class="bd" x1="249" y1="55" x2="270" y2="55"/>
  <line class="lg" x1="235" y1="69" x2="235" y2="92"/>
  <text class="lbl" x="310" y="60">rest</text>
  <text class="lbl" x="310" y="105">SVD, truncate</text>
  <text class="lbl" x="385" y="60">⇒</text>
  <circle class="nd" cx="450" cy="55" r="14"/>
  <circle class="nd" cx="510" cy="55" r="14"/>
  <rect class="box" x="545" y="30" width="60" height="50" rx="4"/>
  <line class="bd" x1="450" y1="55" x2="545" y2="55"/>
  <line class="lg" x1="450" y1="69" x2="450" y2="92"/>
  <line class="lg" x1="510" y1="69" x2="510" y2="92"/>
  <text class="lbl" x="530" y="105">repeat</text>
</svg>
:::

- Reshape, SVD, split off one tensor, repeat along the chain
- Truncating small singular values is **quasi-optimal**: within $\sqrt{n-1}$ of the best rank-$\chi$ approximation [@oseledets2011]
- Needs the dense $2^n$ vector, so small $n$ only. Part II builds without it

## Canonical Forms and Rounding

::: tn
<svg viewBox="0 0 620 120" role="img" aria-label="Mixed canonical form: left-orthogonal tensors, an orthogonality centre, right-orthogonal tensors">
  <line class="bd" x1="70" y1="50" x2="550" y2="50"/>
  <polygon class="nd" points="58,38 82,50 58,62"/>
  <polygon class="nd" points="158,38 182,50 158,62"/>
  <circle class="nd2" cx="290" cy="50" r="16"/>
  <polygon class="nd" points="422,38 398,50 422,62"/>
  <polygon class="nd" points="552,38 528,50 552,62"/>
  <text class="lbl" x="120" y="95">left-orthogonal</text>
  <text class="lbl" x="290" y="95">centre</text>
  <text class="lbl" x="470" y="95">right-orthogonal</text>
</svg>
:::

- Gauge freedom: insert $GG^{-1}$ on any bond, nothing changes
- QR sweeps fix it: left / right / mixed canonical form
- Payoff: truncation is optimal, inner products cheap
- **Rounding** is the workhorse. Products give $\chi_1\chi_2$, so recompress every step

## The Quantics Trick

::: tn
<svg viewBox="0 0 640 150" role="img" aria-label="Grid index written in binary digits, each digit becoming one tensor carrying one length scale">
  <text class="lbl" x="80" y="30">x = 0.i₁i₂i₃…iₙ</text>
  <rect class="box" x="30" y="50" width="120" height="46" rx="4"/>
  <text class="lbl" x="90" y="79">2ⁿ vector</text>
  <text class="lbl" x="180" y="79">⇒</text>
  <line class="bd" x1="240" y1="72" x2="580" y2="72"/>
  <circle class="nd" cx="240" cy="72" r="14"/>
  <circle class="nd" cx="325" cy="72" r="14"/>
  <circle class="nd" cx="410" cy="72" r="14"/>
  <circle class="nd" cx="495" cy="72" r="14"/>
  <circle class="nd" cx="580" cy="72" r="14"/>
  <line class="lg" x1="240" y1="86" x2="240" y2="106"/>
  <line class="lg" x1="325" y1="86" x2="325" y2="106"/>
  <line class="lg" x1="410" y1="86" x2="410" y2="106"/>
  <line class="lg" x1="495" y1="86" x2="495" y2="106"/>
  <line class="lg" x1="580" y1="86" x2="580" y2="106"/>
  <text class="lbl-sm" x="240" y="126">coarsest</text>
  <text class="lbl-sm" x="410" y="126">…</text>
  <text class="lbl-sm" x="580" y="126">finest</text>
  <text class="lbl-sm" x="410" y="42">one tensor per length scale</text>
</svg>
:::

- Index a grid point by binary digits: $x = \sum_{k=1}^{n} i_k 2^{-k}$
- Reshape length-$2^n$ vector into an $n$-leg tensor, write as MPS
- Bond between legs $k$ and $k+1$ measures coupling **between scales**

## Which Functions Are Low-Rank?

| Function | QTT rank |
|---|---|
| $e^{ax}$ | $\chi = 1$ |
| $\sin(ax+b)$, $\cos(ax+b)$ | $\chi = 2$ |
| polynomial, degree $p$ | $\chi = p+1$ |
| sum of $m$ exponentials | $\chi \le m$ |

- Sums and products stay low-rank: ranks add, multiply, then round [@oseledets2013functions]
- Rank tracks **smoothness and scale separation, not resolution**
- Doubling resolution adds one tensor: $O(n)$ parameters, not $O(2^n)$

- Two physical legs per tensor, in and out
- Shift, first derivative, Laplacian: exact MPOs, $\chi_{\text{MPO}} = 2\text{--}4$ [@kazeev2012laplace]

## Heat Equation: Setup

$$\partial_t u = \alpha\,\partial_x^2 u, \qquad x \in [0,1], \qquad N = 2^n$$

- $u^0$ as MPS, discrete Laplacian $L$ as MPO, one scalar $\alpha\Delta t/\Delta x^2$
- Diffusion smooths, so ranks should stay flat. Easiest possible test

## Heat Equation: One Timestep

$$u^{k+1} = \left(\mathbb{1} + \alpha\Delta t\, L\right) u^{k}$$

- Two operations: MPO--MPS product, then **round** to tolerance $\varepsilon$
- Cost $O(n\chi^3)$ per step, memory $O(n\chi^2)$: logarithmic in mesh size
- Skip the rounding and ranks double every step, back to $2^n$

## Heat Equation: What to Watch

- Stability unchanged by compression: $\alpha\Delta t/\Delta x^2 \le 1/2$ with $\Delta x = 2^{-n}$
- Two error sources: discretization $O(\Delta t, \Delta x^2)$ and truncation. Track both
- $\chi(t)$ should stay flat or fall
- Higher-order alternatives: TT time integrators with rank adaptivity [@lubich2015timeint]

## Solving $Ax = b$ in Tensor Format

- $A$ an MPO, $b$ an MPS, $x$ sought as MPS of bond dimension $\chi$
- $A^{-1}$ has no reason to be low-rank. Do not invert
- Minimize over the MPS manifold instead

$$\min_x \|Ax - b\|^2 \qquad\text{or}\qquad \min_x \tfrac12 x^\top\! A x - x^\top b \;\;(A \succ 0)$$

- Manifold is not a vector space, so optimize one tensor at a time

## Sweeping Solvers: ALS and DMRG

::: tn
<svg viewBox="0 0 620 150" role="img" aria-label="One-site and two-site sweeps: a local block is optimized while the rest of the chain is fixed">
  <line class="bd" x1="70" y1="45" x2="550" y2="45"/>
  <circle class="nd" cx="70" cy="45" r="13"/><circle class="nd" cx="166" cy="45" r="13"/>

  <line class="bd" x1="70" y1="115" x2="550" y2="115"/>
  <circle class="nd" cx="70" cy="115" r="13"/><circle class="nd" cx="166" cy="115" r="13"/>

  <text class="lbl" x="311" y="12">two-site: SVD-split after solve, χ adapts</text>

:::

- **ALS / one-site**: freeze all but one tensor, exact small dense solve, sweep [@holtz2012als]
- Objective decreases monotonically, but $\chi$ is fixed in advance
- **Two-site**: optimize a pair, SVD-split, $\chi$ adapts. Local cost to $O(\chi^6)$

## AMEn and Krylov Alternatives

- **AMEn**: one-site sweeps enriched with residual directions. Adaptive rank at one-site cost [@dolgov2014amen]
- **Krylov in TT** (CG, GMRES with rounding): easy to build on TT arithmetic
- Rank growth per iteration is severe, so truncate hard
- Rule: sweeping for structured PDE operators, Krylov for black-box operators

<!-- BEGIN generated: slide refs -->
::: slide-refs
[<span class="ref-n">22</span>]&nbsp;Dolgov & Savostyanov (2014)
:::
<!-- END generated: slide refs -->

## What the Solve Actually Costs

DMRG-type Poisson solve dominates the incompressible solver [@peddinti2024cfd]:

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Share of total runtime | **80.1%** |
| Worst-case local cost | $O(n\chi^6)$ |
| Observed total cost | $O(n\chi^{4.1})$ |

- Gap between worst case and observed is where the knobs live
- Knobs: sweep count, local tolerance, rank cap, warm start from previous step

<!-- BEGIN generated: slide refs -->
::: slide-refs
[<span class="ref-n">13</span>]&nbsp;Peddinti *et al.* (2024)
:::
<!-- END generated: slide refs -->

## Implicit Euler: Why Bother

$$\left(\mathbb{1} - \alpha\Delta t\, L\right) u^{k+1} = u^{k}$$

- Linear solve per step instead of matrix--vector product. More work per step
- Unconditionally stable: $\Delta t$ set by accuracy, not by $\Delta x^2$
- $\Delta x = 2^{-n}$ with $n \gtrsim 20$ makes the explicit bound unusable

## Implicit Euler: Assembling and Solving

- $A = \mathbb{1} - \alpha\Delta t\, L$ as an MPO of rank $\approx 3$, written analytically [@kazeev2012laplace]
- Right-hand side is the previous state MPS
- Solve with DMRG or AMEn, **warm-started from $u^k$**: one or two sweeps
- Compare total wall-clock to a target error, never per-step cost

<!-- BEGIN generated: slide refs -->
::: slide-refs
[<span class="ref-n">19</span>]&nbsp;Kazeev & Khoromskij (2012)
:::
<!-- END generated: slide refs -->

## Implicit Euler: Error Budget

Three sources, not two:

1. time discretization, $O(\Delta t)$
2. space discretization, $O(\Delta x^2)$
3. **solver residual**, under your control

. . .

- Keep residual well below the discretization errors
- Otherwise you converge efficiently to the wrong answer
- Same solve returns as the pressure-Poisson step in Part III

## Three Routes to a QTT

| Route | Cost | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Analytic cores | free | closed form [@oseledets2013functions] |
| TT-SVD | $O(2^n)$ | dense vector |
| TT-cross / TCI | $O(n\chi^2)$ evaluations | black-box $f$ [@oseledets2010ttcross] |

- Third route is the one that scales, and the one that makes the method practical

- Rank-$r$ matrix is exact from $r$ well-chosen rows and columns

## TT-Cross in Practice

1. choose bit ordering, interleaved or stacked
2. set tolerance
3. sweep until cross error plateaus
4. round

. . .

**Failure modes**

- discontinuous $f$: rank blow-up
- bad pivots: features missed entirely
- noisy $f$: the cross interpolates the noise faithfully

## The Problem with Sharp Boundaries

- Immersed object on a $2^n$ mesh, without touching $2^n$ cells
- Natural object is an indicator $\theta(q(x))$: 1 inside, 0 outside
- Step edge has slowly decaying singular values, so $\chi$ explodes
- Fix: give up the sharp edge on purpose, and bound the cost

## Smoothed Masks

$$m(x) = 1 - e^{-\alpha\left(q(x) + |q(x)|\right)}, \qquad q|_{\partial\Omega} = 0$$

- $\alpha$ trades sharpness against rank
- $\ell_2$ distance to the true indicator scales as $\sqrt{\ell_0^{D-2}/\alpha}$ in $D$ dimensions
- An approximation with a knob and an error bound [@peddinti2024cfd]

<!-- BEGIN generated: slide refs -->
::: slide-refs
[<span class="ref-n">13</span>]&nbsp;Peddinti *et al.* (2024)
:::
<!-- END generated: slide refs -->

## Geometry: Putting It Together

- Build $m$ as MPS by TT-cross to tolerance $\varepsilon$. Cost independent of mesh size
- Apply by elementwise (Hadamard) MPS product each step. No-slip without meshing the body
- Inlet and outlet fold into the differential MPOs via ghost cells
- NACA 0040 airfoil: $\chi = 45$, 18,800 parameters, $27.9\times$ compression

## Open Problems: Ranks and Nonlinearity

- **Rank blow-up**: shocks, sharp interfaces, high-$\mathrm{Re}$ turbulence. Where does the method stop paying?
- **Nonlinearity**: MPS products square $\chi$. Picard linear, Newton quadratic, every iteration re-rounds
- **Error control**: no sharp a-posteriori bound from truncation tolerance to accumulated PDE error
- **TT-cross robustness**: pivot choice is heuristic, no guarantee for noisy or adversarial $f$

## Open Problems: Solvers and Structure

- **Preconditioning in TT format**: largely unsolved, biggest lever on cost
- **Conservation**: SVD truncation breaks mass, energy, $\nabla\cdot\mathbf{v}=0$. Structure-preserving rounding is open
- **Scaling out**: 3D + time, index ordering, memory-bound implementations, distributed sweeps
- **Benchmarking**: honest comparison against tuned multigrid and spectral solvers on equal hardware

## Incompressible Navier--Stokes

$$\partial_t \mathbf{v} + (\mathbf{v}\cdot\nabla)\mathbf{v} = -\frac{1}{\rho}\nabla p + \nu\nabla^2\mathbf{v}, \qquad \nabla\cdot\mathbf{v} = 0$$

Three difficulties, each awkward for a tensor network in a different way:

1. **nonlinear advection**: MPS products, ranks multiply
2. **nonlocal pressure constraint**: global elliptic solve every step
3. **boundary conditions on complex geometry**: sharp features, high rank

## Why Pressure Is the Hard Part

- Pressure is not dynamical. No evolution equation for it
- It is whatever enforces $\nabla\cdot\mathbf{v}=0$ instantly. A constraint, not a dynamics
- Divergence of the momentum equation gives an elliptic Poisson problem

$$\nabla^2 p = -\rho\,\nabla\cdot\!\left[(\mathbf{v}\cdot\nabla)\mathbf{v}\right]$$

- Couples the whole domain at once. This is where the runtime goes, classical or tensor

## Reynolds Number and the Cascade

::: tn
<svg viewBox="0 0 620 150" role="img" aria-label="Energy cascade from the integral scale through the inertial range to the Kolmogorov scale">
  <line class="lg" x1="60" y1="95" x2="560" y2="95"/>
  <circle class="nd" cx="90" cy="60" r="26" opacity="0.85"/>
  <circle class="nd" cx="200" cy="66" r="19" opacity="0.75"/>
  <circle class="nd" cx="300" cy="72" r="14" opacity="0.65"/>
  <circle class="nd" cx="390" cy="76" r="10" opacity="0.55"/>
  <circle class="nd" cx="465" cy="80" r="7" opacity="0.45"/>
  <circle class="nd" cx="525" cy="82" r="5" opacity="0.35"/>
  <text class="lbl" x="90" y="122">L &#183; injection</text>
  <text class="lbl" x="300" y="122">inertial range</text>
  <text class="lbl" x="525" y="122">η &#183; dissipation</text>
  <text class="lbl-sm" x="310" y="26">η ~ L·Re⁻³ᐟ⁴</text>
</svg>
:::

- $\mathrm{Re} = UL/\nu$, inertial over viscous forces
- Resolving both ends in 3D needs $\sim\mathrm{Re}^{9/4}$ degrees of freedom
- Aircraft at cruise sits near $\mathrm{Re}\sim10^7$. That is why DNS is impossible

## Benchmarks

| Case | Tests |
|---|---|
| Lid-driven cavity | closed domain, no geometry |
| Flow past cylinder | steady pair, then Kármán street |
| NACA 0040 airfoil | non-trivial immersed geometry |
| Decaying isotropic turbulence | rank behaviour at high $\mathrm{Re}$ |

- Compressible cousin (Euler, shocks, nonlinear flux) targeted separately [@peddinti2025compressible]

## QTT-CFD: Encoding

- Each velocity and pressure component: one MPS over $n = n_x + n_y\,(+\,n_z)$ quantics bits
- Bits interleaved across coordinates, so each scale stays local in the chain
- Gradient, divergence, Laplacian: MPOs of rank 2--4, built once [@kazeev2012laplace]
- Everything downstream is MPO application, Hadamard product, rounding

<!-- BEGIN generated: slide refs -->
::: slide-refs
[<span class="ref-n">19</span>]&nbsp;Kazeev & Khoromskij (2012)
:::
<!-- END generated: slide refs -->

## QTT-CFD: Chorin Projection

::: tn
<svg viewBox="0 0 640 120" role="img" aria-label="Three stages of the projection method: predictor, pressure Poisson solve, projection">
  <rect class="box" x="20" y="30" width="150" height="52" rx="5"/>
  <text class="lbl" x="95" y="52">predictor</text>
  <text class="lbl-sm" x="95" y="70">MPO + Hadamard</text>
  <line class="bd" x1="176" y1="56" x2="216" y2="56"/>
  <rect class="box" x="222" y="30" width="180" height="52" rx="5"/>
  <text class="lbl" x="312" y="52">pressure Poisson</text>
  <text class="lbl-sm" x="312" y="70">DMRG solve &#183; 80% runtime</text>
  <line class="bd" x1="408" y1="56" x2="448" y2="56"/>
  <rect class="box" x="454" y="30" width="160" height="52" rx="5"/>
  <text class="lbl" x="534" y="52">projection</text>
  <text class="lbl-sm" x="534" y="70">restore ∇·v = 0</text>
  <text class="lbl-sm" x="320" y="106">round after every stage</text>
</svg>
:::

$$\mathbf{v}^{*} = \mathbf{v}^{t} + \Delta t\left(-(\mathbf{v}^t\!\cdot\!\nabla)\mathbf{v}^t + \nu\nabla^2\mathbf{v}^t\right)$$
$$\nabla^2 p = \tfrac{\rho}{\Delta t}\nabla\!\cdot\!\mathbf{v}^{*}, \qquad \mathbf{v}^{t+1} = \mathbf{v}^{*} - \tfrac{\Delta t}{\rho}\nabla p$$

Scheme after [@chorin1968], in tensor form [@peddinti2024cfd].

[<span class="ref-n">13</span>]&nbsp;Peddinti *et al.* (2024) · [<span class="ref-n">24</span>]&nbsp;Chorin (1968)
:::
<!-- END generated: slide refs -->

## QTT-CFD: Geometry and Readout

- Smoothed MPS mask applied elementwise after the predictor
- Ghost-cell inlet and outlet live inside the MPOs
- Readout without decompression:
  - coarse-grained field $O(n\chi^3)$
  - single pixel $O(\chi^3)$
- Dense $2^n$ vector never reconstructed. Without this the compression buys nothing

## QTT-CFD: Results and Scaling

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Mesh (cylinder) | $2^{30}$ cells |
| Bond dimension | $\chi = 30$ |
| Parameters | 24,200 |
| Compression | $\sim\!4.4\times10^{4}$ |
| Reynolds range | 1.7 -- 2230 |
| Observed runtime | $\sim n\chi^{4.1}$ |

- Poly-logarithmic in mesh size, validated against Ansys Fluent on squared geometries [@peddinti2024cfd]

## Other Frameworks

- **Reduced-order models**, wall-bounded flow at a few % of DNS variables [@kiffner2023rom]
- **Turbulence PDFs** computed directly in TN form [@gourianov2025pdf]
- **Vlasov--Poisson**, kinetic plasma [@ye2022vlasov]
- **Lattice Boltzmann** in TT form: different discretization, same compression idea
- Common thread: ansatz is portable, the global solve is always the hard part

## Fluid Dynamics Is Where the Cycles Go

- CFD is a top consumer of HPC: aerodynamics, weather, climate, combustion, biomedical flow
- Bottleneck is resolution, and resolution costs $\sim\mathrm{Re}^{9/4}$ in 3D
- Exascale still cannot do a full aircraft at flight Reynolds number
- RANS and LES are models: tuned closures, limited transfer between regimes

## Why It Suits Tensor Networks

- Turbulence is a cascade. Well-separated scales couple weakly [@gourianov2022]
- Quantics gives a scale-by-scale representation for free
- Physics hierarchy and ansatz hierarchy are the same hierarchy
- Honest stress test: nonlinear, multiscale, complex geometry, quantitative benchmarks
- Same encoding is the natural interface to future quantum CFD

<!-- BEGIN generated: slide refs -->
::: slide-refs
[<span class="ref-n">9</span>]&nbsp;Gourianov *et al.* (2022)
:::
<!-- END generated: slide refs -->

## Expressivity: The Question

- Everything so far assumed $\chi$ stays small. When is that true?
- Two sub-questions with different answers:
  - $\chi$ versus **resolution** at fixed physics: benign, that is the quantics promise
  - $\chi$ versus **Reynolds number**: the real question
- Empirical answer follows, 3D turbulence [@pisoni2026turbulence]

<!-- BEGIN generated: slide refs -->
::: slide-refs
[<span class="ref-n">14</span>]&nbsp;Pisoni *et al.* (2026)
:::
<!-- END generated: slide refs -->

## Expressivity: 3D Turbulence at $\mathrm{Re}_\lambda = 315$

DNS on $1024^3 = 2^{30}$ points, encoded as 30-tensor trains:

| $\chi$ | Parameters kept | What survives |
|---|---|---|
| 1000 | 2.2% | full flat inertial range of $E(k)$ |
| 100 | 0.03% | stable solver for 9--10 turnover times |

- Four orders of magnitude of compression, spectrum essentially intact

## Expressivity: What Breaks First

- Spectrum is the easy diagnostic. It looks fine long after the flow does not
- Demanding diagnostics: **PDFs of velocity increments** and **flatness**
- Stacked ordering over-smooths at low $\chi$. Interleaved keeps non-Gaussian statistics
- Below $\chi \approx 500$ interleaved injects spurious small-scale fluctuations
- Both encodings fail, differently

## Expressivity: The Honest Claim

- Supported: turbulence compresses well at **moderate** $\mathrm{Re}$
- Not supported: low rank at arbitrary $\mathrm{Re}$ and every scale
- $\chi = 100$ ceiling in the 3D solver is memory-bound implementation, not physics
- Flip side: random low-rank TTs ($\chi=10$) cascaded across scales synthesize divergence-free turbulent-like fields, correct spectrum and flatness, at logarithmic cost

## Outlook: Solvers and Scale

- **Higher $\mathrm{Re}$, full 3D**: lifting $\chi = 100$ is engineering before physics
- **Better solvers**: TT preconditioning, distributed sweeps, mixed precision. Poisson is 80% of runtime
- **Adaptivity**: pick $\chi(t)$ and $\Delta t$ from a live error estimate [@lubich2015timeint]
- **Structure-preserving truncation**: keep $\nabla\cdot\mathbf{v}=0$ and conserved quantities under rounding

<!-- BEGIN generated: slide refs -->
::: slide-refs
[<span class="ref-n">20</span>]&nbsp;Lubich *et al.* (2015)
:::
<!-- END generated: slide refs -->

## Outlook: Physics and Theory

- **Compressible and multiphysics**: shocks, reacting flow, MHD. Rank behaviour unmapped
- **Theory gap**: no sharp rank bounds for Navier--Stokes solutions versus $\mathrm{Re}$
- **Hybrid TN + ML**: learned closures, learned preconditioners, TN surrogates. Part IV
- **Quantum hand-off**: same MPS encoding feeds future quantum CFD algorithms

## When the PDE Is Unknown

- Parts I--III: equation known, solution wanted. Now invert that
- Available: snapshots $\{u(t_k)\}$ from experiment, DNS, or sensors
- Missing: the operator, the closure, sometimes the equation
- Regime of most measurement data, and of systems too complex to write down

## Two Tasks, Kept Separate

| Task | Goal | Interpretable model |
|---|---|---|
| Prediction | forecast $u(t_{K+k})$ | not required |
| Identification | recover operator or equations | the entire point |

- Methods strong at one are often weak at the other
- Classical toolkit: POD/PCA, DMD and Koopman, SINDy [@brunton2016sindy], operator learning, data assimilation

<!-- BEGIN generated: slide refs -->
::: slide-refs
[<span class="ref-n">25</span>]&nbsp;Brunton *et al.* (2016)
:::
<!-- END generated: slide refs -->

## The Same Curse, Again

- Snapshot matrix is $N_x \times N_t$ with $N_x = 2^n$. Even the SVD is prohibitive
- Data adds its own problems: sparse, noisy, short series, non-stationary, no guaranteed closed model
- Tensor-network promise: compress space **and** time, do the algebra inside the format, keep modes interpretable
- Model in MPS format feeds straight back into the Part III solver

## Dynamic Mode Decomposition

$$u_{k+1} \approx A\,u_k$$

- Find best linear $A$ from data, read off eigenpairs [@schmid2010dmd]
- Eigenvalue gives growth rate and frequency. Eigenvector gives a spatial mode
- Output is a set of individually interpretable structures

<!-- BEGIN generated: slide refs -->
::: slide-refs
[<span class="ref-n">26</span>]&nbsp;Schmid (2010)
:::
<!-- END generated: slide refs -->

## The Standard DMD Recipe

$$X = [u_0 \cdots u_{T-1}], \quad X' = [u_1 \cdots u_T], \quad X = U\Sigma V^\dagger$$
$$\tilde{A} = U^\dagger X' V \Sigma^{-1}, \quad \tilde{A} = W\Lambda W^{-1}, \quad \Phi = UW$$

- Koopman view: finite-rank approximation of the linear infinite-dimensional Koopman operator on observables [@tu2014dmd]
- That is why a linear method describes nonlinear dynamics

<!-- BEGIN generated: slide refs -->
::: slide-refs
[<span class="ref-n">27</span>]&nbsp;Tu *et al.* (2014)
:::
<!-- END generated: slide refs -->

## Space-Time in a Single MPS

::: tn

  <line class="cut" x1="325" y1="20" x2="325" y2="90"/>

- Binarize **both** $x$ and $t$ into one MPS [@peddinti2025spacetime]
- Time stops being a loop, becomes more legs on the same chain
- Space-then-time works generally. Time-then-space converged better for nonlinear Schrödinger
- Temporal bond dimension measures temporal complexity directly

## The All-at-Once Solve

- Assemble the whole space-time system as one MPO, solve once with DMRG. No time loop
- Nonlinear terms by Picard iteration. Linear convergence, Newton would give quadratic

| Equation | $\chi$ | Compression |
|---|---|---|
| Heat, wave | 2 -- 22 | $> 99\%$ |
| Burgers, nonlinear diffusion | 10 | $> 99\%$, residual $\sim\!10^{-3}$ |

On a $1024\times1024$ space-time grid [@peddinti2025spacetime].

## MPS-DMD: The Idea

- Standard DMD needs an SVD of an $N_x \times N_t$ matrix. That is the bottleneck
- The space-time MPS **already contains** that SVD. Gauge it into the right form
- Run the whole DMD pipeline inside the MPS, never forming the snapshot matrix
- Same modes, same eigenvalues, same predictions, exponentially cheaper
- Earlier tensor DMD variants stayed linear in $N_t$ [@klus2018tdmd]

<!-- BEGIN generated: slide refs -->
::: slide-refs
[<span class="ref-n">28</span>]&nbsp;Klus *et al.* (2018)
:::
<!-- END generated: slide refs -->

## MPS-DMD: Three Steps

::: tn
<svg viewBox="0 0 620 130" role="img" aria-label="Mixed canonical gauge at the space-time bond yields the SVD factors directly">
  <line class="bd" x1="60" y1="48" x2="540" y2="48"/>
  <polygon class="nd" points="48,36 72,48 48,60"/>
  <polygon class="nd" points="148,36 172,48 148,60"/>
  <circle class="nd2" cx="290" cy="48" r="16"/>
  <polygon class="nd" points="422,36 398,48 422,60"/>
  <polygon class="nd" points="542,36 518,48 542,60"/>
  <text class="lbl" x="110" y="90">U</text>
  <text class="lbl" x="290" y="90">Σ</text>
  <text class="lbl" x="470" y="90">V†</text>
  <text class="lbl-sm" x="290" y="118">Schmidt decomposition at the space/time bond</text>
</svg>
:::

1. **Gauge** to mixed canonical form at the space/time bond. The Schmidt decomposition *is* $U\Sigma V^\dagger$
2. **Project**: $\tilde{A} = U^\dagger A U$, a $\chi\times\chi$ matrix
3. **Eigendecompose** $\tilde{A} = W\Lambda W^{-1}$, modes $\Phi = UW$, predict by local contraction

$$u_{T+k} = A^k u_T = U W \Lambda^k W^{-1} U^\dagger u_T$$

## MPS-DMD: Results

Runtime **logarithmic in both $N_x$ and $N_t$**.

| Case | Setup | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Burgers | $\chi = 10$, $1024^2$ | accurate 1000 steps ahead at 99% compression |
| 2D cylinder wake | $256\times128\times1024$, 25-bit MPS, $\chi=200$ | 97.42% compression, 100 modes capture the street |

- External data: stack snapshot MPSs sequentially, truncate after each. Linear in timestep count

## Outlook: Extending the Method

- **Beyond (1+1)D**: analysis is 1D in space. 2D/3D + time and its index ordering is open
- **Koopman extensions**: extended DMD with TT dictionaries, kernel DMD compressed
- **Equation discovery**: SINDy in TT form over tensor-product dictionaries [@brunton2016sindy; @klus2018tdmd]
- **Noise**: truncation can denoise, or fit the noise. No theory yet
- **Streaming**: update the MPS as data arrives, no recompression from scratch

## Outlook: Practice and Positioning

- **Hybrid physics + data**: Part III solver as prior, learn only the closure or residual in TT form
- **Uncertainty quantification**: error bars on TN predictions essentially absent
- **Interpretability** is the edge over neural surrogates. Modes, frequencies, growth rates come out directly
- **Software**: shared TT/MPS tooling [@nunez2025tci], standard benchmarks, open datasets

# Appendix {background-color="#bc6c16"}

## TT-Cross: Algorithm

Build MPS of a black-box $f$ from $O(n\chi^2)$ evaluations.

1. Initialize pivot sets $\mathcal{I}_k$ (rows), $\mathcal{J}_k$ (columns) per bond
2. Sweep left to right: form the $\chi\!\times\!2\chi$ slice $F_k = f(\mathcal{I}_k, i_k, \mathcal{J}_k)$
3. **maxvol** on $F_k$: pick $\chi$ rows of maximum $|\det|$, update $\mathcal{I}_{k+1}$
4. Core $= F_k \hat{F}_k^{-1}$, carry the residual right
5. Sweep back, repeat until the cross error plateaus

. . .

- Interpolation property: the MPS is **exact** on all sampled fibres
- maxvol submatrix within $(r+1)$ of the true maximum volume, greedily
- Rank-adaptive variants add pivots where the local error is largest [@nunez2025tci]

## DMRG: Two-Site Sweep

::: tn
<svg viewBox="0 0 640 140" role="img" aria-label="Two-site DMRG: contract a pair, solve locally, split by SVD, move the centre">
  <line class="bd" x1="40" y1="45" x2="240" y2="45"/>
  <circle class="nd" cx="40" cy="45" r="12"/><circle class="nd2" cx="120" cy="45" r="14"/>
  <circle class="nd2" cx="180" cy="45" r="14"/><circle class="nd" cx="240" cy="45" r="12"/>
  <text class="lbl-sm" x="150" y="80">contract pair</text>
  <text class="lbl" x="290" y="50">⇒</text>
  <rect class="nd2" x="330" y="30" width="46" height="30" rx="4"/>
  <text class="lbl-sm" x="353" y="80">solve local</text>
  <text class="lbl" x="415" y="50">⇒</text>
  <line class="bd" x1="460" y1="45" x2="600" y2="45"/>
  <circle class="nd" cx="460" cy="45" r="12"/><circle class="nd" cx="520" cy="45" r="12"/>
  <circle class="nd2" cx="580" cy="45" r="14"/><circle class="nd" cx="600" cy="45" r="12"/>
  <text class="lbl-sm" x="530" y="80">SVD split, centre moves</text>
</svg>
:::

- Local problem: eigenproblem (ground state) or linear solve ($Ax=b$)
- Effective operator from cached left and right environments, updated per site
- SVD split sets $\chi$ from a truncation tolerance, so rank **adapts**
- Cost $O(n\chi^3 d^2 + n\chi^2 d\,\chi_{\text{MPO}})$ per sweep, local solve up to $O(\chi^6)$
- Two-site escapes local minima that trap one-site; AMEn recovers this at one-site cost [@dolgov2014amen; @holtz2012als]
